notes: YOUR BACKUPS SHOULD SURVIVE YOUR COMPUTER. A backup folder on the same computer as your books is not a backup: one theft, one dead disk, and the ledger and every copy of it go together. MoRaj Ledger now checks whether the destination you chose actually survives this machine — a cloud folder such as OneDrive or Google Drive, or a separate drive — and tells you when it does not, instead of showing a reassuring tick over a folder that would be lost with everything else. GOING LIVE NOW ASKS YOU TO SET UP BACKUPS FIRST. Once, at the moment your books start to matter. Trying the app out in UAT is unaffected — that is what UAT is for. AUTOMATIC BACKUPS NOW RUN HOURLY, NOT ONLY WHEN YOU SIGN IN. If the program stays open all week, that used to be one attempt a week. A CLOUD FOLDER WITH NO PASSPHRASE leaves your full ledger — salaries included — readable to anyone with access to that cloud account. That warning now stays on screen until you set one. PRINT A BACKUP RECOVERY SHEET. Backup & Export → Print recovery sheet gives you one page with everything the person restoring your books will need: where the backups are, the steps, and the organisation name the restore is checked against — with a ruled line to write your passphrase on BY HAND. It never prints the passphrase itself, because a print dialogue offers Save as PDF and that file's likeliest home is the same cloud folder as your backups. LICENSING. A licence file that cannot be read now says so, and shows your licence ID, rather than telling a paying customer their evaluation has ended. A computer with a wrong clock no longer ends an evaluation permanently — a dead battery or a mistyped year used to be a one-way door, and correcting the clock now brings the trial back. Trial and expiry messages name the dates they are talking about. There is NO database change in this release: your data and settings are untouched, and upgrading is simply installing over the old version.
